FIRPS PHOTOGRAPHS OF EVACUATION OF GALLIPOLI; WOODERFUL FEAT CARRIED OUT UNDER THE NOSSES OF THE TURKS. Photo shows the last scene at Gallipoli. The withdrawal was one of the most wonderful feats in Military history, all guns and howizers being not every with the exception of seventeen worn-out weapons, which were blown up. We withdrew without leaving as much as a wounded men behind. The scene of the evacuation. Tye men left behind them a blaze of burning wrockage, that must have flashed the news across the boat for miles around.

CAGE FLOODS THE SEA FRONT AT SALONIKA: ALLIED WARCHIPS AT THE GINGEIN PORT, ABIG gale was experienced at Salonika when a number of small boats showed were wrecked and the sea front flooded. A glimpse of the Allies' washings off the port. The picture was taken when the storm was at its height.

HOW THE WOUNDED SOLDIERS ARE CONVEYED TO THE HOSPITALS SHIPS. The photograph was taken at the Dardenelles. The wounded are placed on hisspital ships, whence they are conveyed to Egypt or Malta for treatment. Others are sent to England.
Wounded men, who are lying on stretchers, being conveyed across a kink river by the men of the Royal Army Medical Corps, who are punting with branches of trees.
